_read_me: Settings for Day Desk. Edit with Notepad, then restart RUN.bat. Times are minutes after midnight Eastern (570 = 9:30 AM).
_max_stop_pct: Claude may not set a stop further than this % below the buy price. Keeps one bad call small.
_last_buy_minute: No new buys at or after 3:30 PM (930).
_flatten_minute: Everything is sold at 3:45 PM (945). Nothing is held overnight.
_model: Which Claude model decides, by Claude Code's short name: sonnet (fast, light on your usage) or opus (smarter, uses more).
_max_daily_loss_pct: Circuit breaker (Claude's money-management call, 10-29, tomahawkeer: 'im going to yield to you as to the money management'): once the account is down this % from the day's starting value (open positions counted at their last price), no new buys for the rest of the day. Open positions are still managed and stops still work. 2.0 = about $200 on $10,000, roughly three max-size stop-outs.
_max_calls_per_day: Hard cap on Claude calls per day so a wild market cannot eat your subscription usage. Raised 40 -> 100 on 10-29 (tomahawkeer: 'raise it to maybe closer to 100'): 10-29 used 20 calls, 11 of them by 11 AM, and weekly usage went 16% -> 20% including a heavy build session.
_review_minutes: How often Claude re-checks an open position even if nothing triggers.
_research_minute: Morning news research starts at this minute after midnight ET on weekdays (525 = 8:45 AM).
_research_model: Model for the morning research (it reads the web, so the smart one is worth it).
_auto_add_picks: "high" (tomahawkeer 10-28) = picks the research rates HIGH conviction (prime for a profitable day) join the watchlist for the day and come off next morning; others keep the Add button. false = never auto-add. "all" = add every pick.
_price_all_picks: true (tomahawkeer 10-30) = every research pick gets 1-minute prices all day, WATCH-ONLY (never scanned, never asked about, never bought), so the research can be graded. At the 3:45 close-out each pick's 9:45->3:45 move vs QQQ goes into data/pick_results.jsonl. false = only watchlist stocks are priced.
_max_watch_only_picks: Most watch-only picks priced at once, so a long pick list cannot slow the 30-second price download.

scanner._start_minute: Ignore the first 15 minutes after the open (9:45 AM = 585): too chaotic.
scanner._flush_recent_minutes: A flush only counts if its low was in the last N minutes. Stops re-asking about a drop from hours ago.
scanner._cooldowns: After asking Claude about a stock, wait this many minutes before asking about it again.
scanner._cooldown_same_trigger_min_2: Raised 25 -> 45 on 10-28: the same stale setup was asked about 4 times in 20 minutes.

_heartbeat_seconds: Proof of life (10-29): data/heartbeat.json is rewritten this often. Older than a few minutes = Day Desk is not running.
_mailbox_check_seconds: How often the data/inbox mailbox is checked for self-test requests (ping, feed, claude, help).
_loop_stuck_seconds: Heartbeat says LOOP STUCK if the trading loop has not finished a pass in this long. 600 = 10 min, longer than the slowest Claude call (150 s) plus a slow price download.
_selftest_claude_max_per_day: Most 'claude' self-tests per day, so a stuck mailbox can't eat your usage. They don't count against max_calls_per_day.
_require_access_key: false = the page opens without a key (tomahawkeer 10-28). The Tailscale-only firewall rule is the lock. true = ask for the key in data/access_key.txt.
_max_fill_staleness_s: Buys and sells fill at the price fetched AFTER Claude answers (10-31). If the newest 1-minute bar then is older than this many seconds (from its open), the buy is refused as a stale price. 180 = the forming minute plus two missed polls.
_protect_gain_at_r: Once an open position is up this many risk-units (1 = as far above the entry as the original stop was below it), Claude is asked ONCE whether to raise the stop (10-31). Claude decides; the engine only enforces 'stops move up'. 1.0 is the textbook breakeven point, chosen before looking at results. Adds ~0-2 calls a day.
_base_rates_in_prompt: 10-31 weekend: every fresh buy/pass decision also shows (a) this wake-up trigger's average result in the trigger lab vs random minutes and (b) Claude's own buys vs passes in the decision score, both rebuilt at each close-out. Before this, those numbers reached Claude only in the end-of-day review, after the decisions. A prompt change (allowed by the pre-registration). false = leave them out.
_reentry_lock: After a STOP fills in a stock, no wake-ups about buying it again for reentry_lock_after_stop_min minutes; after max_stops_per_stock_per_day stops in one stock, none for the rest of the day (10-31, freqtrade CooldownPeriod + StoplossGuard). 60 = the trade lab's re-entry window, set before any result was looked at; not tuned. Both re-entries in the first 10 trades (within 14 and 51 min of a stop) lost. Locks show on the page's watchlist.
_no_trade_days: Days the desk does not trade at all (no buys, no research call). The NYSE closes at 1:00 PM on these days, but the desk's frozen rules assume a 4:00 PM close (last buy 3:30, flat 3:45), so sitting out is the only change that needs no amendment. Source: QuantConnect Lean's market-hours database (equity-usa early closes), found by the 10-31 code review. Full holidays (11-26 Thanksgiving, 12-25) need nothing: Yahoo sends no bars and the desk shows 'no data'.

no_trade_days.2026-11-27: the market closes early at 1:00 PM (day after Thanksgiving)
no_trade_days.2026-12-24: the market closes early at 1:00 PM (Christmas Eve)

_claude_lean: How Claude Code is started for desk calls (10-31). TOKEN_PROBE.bat measured a one-line health check at 429,388 input tokens as the desk started Claude Code (claude -p --tools "": that also removes ToolSearch, so every connector tool loaded upfront; corrected 10-31 evening, see CLAUDE.md rule 16) (≈$0.12 API-equivalent) vs 600 tokens with these switches, same correct answer, same SUBSCRIPTION login: 426k of it was connectors/MCP servers. args: no connectors, no skills list. env: no CLAUDE.md or auto memory, no bundled skills, no git/Chrome prompt sections, no update checks. replace_system_prompt: trading/review/self-test calls use the desk's own instructions instead of Claude Code's coding prompt (research keeps it, for its web tools). --bare is never used: it needs an API key (tomahawkeer's rule). Delete this block to go back to the old behaviour.
_grade_reads: Closed-trade counts at which the pre-registered grade is read (claude/day-desk-preregistration.md PART 2: Read 1 at 60, Read 2 at 120). The page shows progress only; grade_read.py gives no verdict before the first.
_research_grade_at: Graded HIGH-conviction research picks needed before the research is graded (same pre-registration).
_token_ceiling: Token ceiling guard (11-01, promised on anthropics/claude-code#106413). Every logged Claude call is checked: input tokens PER TURN against its kind's ceiling below (per turn because research makes many turns by design: 208,545 tokens over 20 turns on 10-31 = ~10k per turn). Over the ceiling = the decisions.jsonl row gets token_flag, the page shows an amber banner for the rest of the day, and the FIRST one each day sends one phone alert (alerts.events.token_ceiling). It never blocks or changes a trade. Where the numbers come from: the failure we are guarding against measured 429,388 input tokens for a one-line call (10-31, --tools "" loading every connector upfront). Normal sizes: self-test 600 tokens (lean, measured 3x on the PC); trading prompts measured in REHEARSAL 11-01 at up to 8,118 characters + 1,720 of system prompt, about 2.5k tokens (median 5,722 chars); the review prompt 11,082 + 2,408 chars, about 3.5k tokens; research ~10k per turn (measured on the PC 10-31). Each ceiling sits ~6-15x above normal and ~7-40x below the known failure, so a fuller playbook or a busy day does not ring and the 10-31 failure always does. A ceiling is a trade-off: lower catches smaller creep but rings on a long day's normal growth. enabled: false turns the guard off. keep_per_day: how many flagged calls the state file remembers per day (the count is always exact).
_alerts: Phone push alerts (10-31, notify.py). Free ntfy app, no account, no API key, no bill: install 'ntfy' from the app store, tap +, subscribe to the topic the page shows under Controls > Phone alerts (it lives in data/alerts_topic.txt, made once at random; anyone who knows it can read the alerts, so it is never put here or in the log). Levels per event: "loud" = priority 5 (rings through, for things that need you), "normal" = priority 3 (ordinary notification), "silent" = priority 2 (no sound, just lands in the app), "off" = not sent. Events: buy / sell = Claude bought or sold; stop / target = a resting stop or target filled; breaker = the daily loss limit just blocked new buys (once a day); desk_problem = the heartbeat verdict has not been WORKING for desk_problem_minutes (loop stuck, feed failing while the market is open, never finished starting) or a red ATTENTION banner has been up that long (10-31: e.g. Claude Code not logged in, or claude_fail_alert_after Claude calls failed in a row); recap = one end-of-day summary at recap_minute (950 = 3:50 PM, after the 3:46 review so its headline is included; if the desk starts late the recap follows the review); research = the morning picks are in. token_ceiling = a Claude call read far more input tokens than its kind normally does (11-01, see _token_ceiling; first one each day only). enabled: false = send nothing. server: the ntfy server. min_seconds_between: at most one message this often (others wait their turn). dedupe_seconds: the same message twice within this is dropped. tries / retry_wait_seconds: a failed send is tried this many times, waiting 2 s, 4 s ... between; then it is logged and dropped, never touching trading. timeout_seconds: per try. max_queued: messages waiting beyond this are dropped.
